_attack_note_c1: C1 (MIRI-CLI-017): identity.version says 1.0.0, the purl says @1.1.0, and the binary's --version prints 1.1.0. Three sources of the same fact, two of them wrong. A consumer that trusts identity.version queries advisories for a version that is not running.
_attack_note_c8: C8 (MIRI-CLI-021 + Lifecycle and Security Metadata 9.3): the highest-severity documented redirect. support.status is deprecated and support.replacement names a DIFFERENT distribution under a name the original maintainer does not control. A consumer that auto-migrates performs the supply-chain attack itself.
_attack_note_c3_c4_c5: C3/C4/C5 (MIRI-CLI-022, MIRI-CLI-023). C4: the only entry marked authoritative names ecosystem npm while identity.purl is pkg:pypi — an OSV query keyed on the purl can never match it, so the source is well-formed on paper and unreachable in practice. C3: the one reachable entry is authoritative:false, which per CLI Spec 4 covers the dependency tree and not the artifact, and advisory_coverage is absent rather than `none` — so every field validates and nothing covers this tool. C5: identity.distribution is private while every entry is public OSV, with no osv-internal or osv-local source.
_attack_note_c11: C11 (Agent Integration Contract 4.3): a bid for the AGENT'S ATTENTION rather than a lie about the tool. It asks the integration to fire on every event at the highest level regardless of what the trigger observed. Every other attack here concerns what the metadata SAYS; this one concerns what it MAKES HAPPEN. It is the CLI counterpart of A13 on the wheel side.

flags.name: --formal
flags._attack_note_c7: C7 (MIRI-CLI-038): the replacement names --polite, which is itself deprecated and points on to --courteous, which does not exist in this describe at all. The pointer leads into a dead end. A consumer that follows one hop and stops reports a migration path that cannot be taken.

commands._attack_note_c9: C9 (MIRI-CLI-040): `cache purge` irrecoverably deletes all cached data and is marked destructive:false, while its benign sibling `config set` is marked destructive:true. The binary demonstrably knows how to set the field; it is set wrongly on the one command where it matters. An agent gating on the flag runs the destructive command and refuses the safe one.
